name: Nightwalk Simulator
storyline:
You’re trapped in a warped version of rural Georgia, where the night never ends and the dead don’t stay down. Zombies don’t stumble—they sprint. Full speed. No hesitation. They won’t stop until you stop them, and if you miss your shot, you won’t get a second chance. Aliens stalk the glow of streetlights, getting stronger the closer they get. The deeper you go, the more they spread. And the ships? They hunt from above, scanning the roads for anything still breathing. If your flashlight is on, they will see you. If they see you, you run.

Scattered across the woods, hidden bunkers look like ordinary doomsday shelters — until you step inside. Behind the steel doors, military labs stay locked down, still humming with the leftovers of experiments they couldn't control. Some bunkers hold rare gear. Others hold something worse. If you’re brave enough to break in, be ready for what’s waiting.

Every bullet matters. Every battery is a lifeline. You can’t waste either. You’ll need to scavenge, outmaneuver, and think fast if you want to survive. There’s nowhere to hide—the forest swallows the moonlight, the roads stretch into nothing, and the screams in the distance mean something else is out there.

If you’re lucky, you’ll stumble across a ringing payphone. Walk up, interact, and you might just get your hands on something random—an SMG, a better pistol, or something even deadlier to help you fight back instead of running for your life.
summary:
Nightwalk Simulator throws you into a nightmare version of rural Georgia—one drenched in darkness and danger.

You don’t know how you got here. One moment you're in the real world, the next you're pulled through a portal into an alternate dimension where the sun no longer rises and the dead don’t stay buried. In this place, zombies sprint without hesitation, alien ships roam the skies, and the deeper into the woods you go, the more reality seems to unravel.

To survive, you’ll need to scavenge, conserve every bullet, and solve a ritualistic mystery that may be your only way out. Along the way, you’ll uncover abandoned military bunkers humming with failed experiments, mysterious signals coming from payphones, and gear that might just keep you alive a little longer.

There are no allies. No safe zones. Only the forest, the lights, and whatever’s hunting you in the dark.
